title: ABV common breeding bird monitoring, Flanders: point counts of 180 bird taxa summed per visit in 757 1 km squares, 2017-2025
creator: Piesschaert, Frederik; Vermeersch, Glenn; Brosens, Dimitri; Westra, Toon; Desmet, Peter; Feys, Sam; Van de Poel, Sander; Pollet, Marc; Cooleman, Stijn (Research Institute for Nature and Forest, INBO)
citation: Piesschaert F, Vermeersch G, Brosens D, Westra T, Desmet P, Feys S, Van de Poel S, Pollet M, Cooleman S (2026). ABV - Common breeding birds in Flanders, Belgium (post 2016). Version 1.23. Research Institute for Nature and Forest (INBO). Sampling event dataset. https://doi.org/10.15468/pj2v6h
abstract: The Flemish common breeding bird monitoring scheme (Algemene Broedvogelmonitoring Vlaanderen, ABV), run by INBO and Natuurpunt Studie with volunteers through Meetnetten.be: up to six random points in each of a stratified random sample of 1 km UTM squares, all counted on one day, three times in a breeding season in fixed windows, five minutes per point, every adult breeding bird seen or heard counted. One row per square-date (a visit) and taxon, y the number of adults counted over the visit's point counts (obs_points_counted gives how many); zeros by complement of the complete count.
samplingProtocol: Five-minute point count of all adult breeding birds seen or heard at up to six random points in a 1 x 1 km UTM square, all points on the same day, three visits a year in fixed windows (1 March-15 April, 16 April-31 May, 1 June-15 July) at least two weeks apart (Vermeersch, Ledegen & Feys 2018); foraging gulls and herons breeding elsewhere and flocks flying over are excluded.
closureNote: occasion = the point's counts within a breeding season (March to mid-July), across which arrivals and breeding change detectability and numbers; period = calendar year; squares are counted in some years only (at least once every three years)
geographicCoverage: Flanders, Belgium (1 km UTM square centroids coarsened to 0.1-degree cell centres)

coordinatesCoarsened.method: coarsen_coords(): the 1 km square centroids INBO publishes snapped to their 0.1-degree cell centre, uncertainty 707 m plus the cell half-diagonal, and the square codes (ABV_<UTM square>) replaced by sequential ids (E7 scope, 4), because IUCN VU species are in the table within their native range (Aythya ferina (VU), Streptopelia turtur (VU); E7, ruling on the publisher 2026-11-06). inbo_2026_flanders_abv_exact_count keeps the other taxa with centroids and square codes as published.

covariateNote: obs_points_counted = number of five-minute point counts made in the square that day (1-6; effort); obs_start_time = start time of the day's first count (HH:MM, local; NA where not recorded).
notes: y sums all records of a taxon over the point counts of one square-date (the app stores groups as separate records; 10234 point-count x taxon pairs had more than one record). The point is not the unit: 598 visits record every point under one locationID, so points cannot be told apart. Three subspecies are their own taxa alongside their species, as recorded. 18 point counts (3 square-dates) are dated January-February, outside the protocol windows, probably day and month swapped in entry; kept as published.

notShipped.square codes: the 1 km square codes (ABV_<UTM square>) locate the square; replaced by sequential ids Q0001.. (E7 scope, 4); inbo_2026_flanders_abv_exact_count has them
notShipped.per-point counts: summed per square-date (point identity is not recoverable in 598 visits)
notShipped.taxa only in dropped surveys: Netta rufina (red-crested pochard), recorded only in a dropped double-entered square-date
notShipped.Humboldt effort fields: person-minutes per visit (5 minutes x points counted; obs_points_counted carries it)
